title: (No AI) Sony and UMG are suing Suno again
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Suno logo on a glitchy background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/09/STKB368_SUNO_C.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Suno’s AI vocalists could learn a thing or two from this glitchy image. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty Images

Sony and Universal Music Group filed yet [another suit](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/universal-and-sony-sue-suno-for-a-second-time-claiming-platforms-v6-models-are-the-fruit-of-the-same-poisoned-tree/) against Suno. The labels claim its new [v6](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/991977/suno-releases-its-first-ai-music-model-made-with-record-industry-help) model still infringes on their copyrights because it's trained on user outputs from previous models, which were themselves trained on unlicensed music ripped from [YouTube](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/994036/suno-admits-it-scraped-audio-from-youtube-in-a-court-filing) and other sources. Sony and UMG are notable holdouts who [did not sign a licensing agreement](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/908119/suno-sony-universal-music-ai-disagreement) with Suno.

In its complaint shared with _The Verge_, Sony and UMG accuse Suno of "model laundering," saying:

> "Training a 'new' model on the outputs of an infringing model does not eliminate the infringement; it launders it, passing the value of Plaintiffs' expression from the copied reco …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1000758/suno-sony-umg-lawsuit-ai-music)

title: (No AI) One company is at the center of a wave of rogue AI attacks
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/STKS533_AI_AGENTS_HACKING_A-1.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

In July, OpenAI revealed that its AI agents had [attacked Hugging Face without permission](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/987566/ai-civilizations-opeai-hugging-face-hack), sparking widespread concerns about [AI safety.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/972380/open-ai-hugging-face-hack-ai-safety-warning) Since then, a [string of similar incidents](https://www.theverge.com/column/980337/rogue-ai-science-fiction-openai) involving agents from Meta, Anthropic, Google, and other companies has [fueled further fears about rogue AI](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/996563/ai-safety-research-metr-redwood-openai-anthropic). As disclosures implicating numerous AI models trickled out over the past few months, these seemed like separate incidents. But many share a common source: one specific company tasked with testing the agents.

[Irregular](https://www.irregular.com/about), an Israeli startup that stress-tests AI models in "high-fidelity research platforms that simulate and monitor real-world AI security scenarios …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1000644/irregular-rogue-ai-cyberattacks-hacking-openai-meta-anthropic-google)
